name: CILEX Level 3 Diploma in Law and Practice (CPQ Foundation Stage)
material_vintage: CILEX Professional Qualification (CPQ) Foundation Stage, the entry stage of CILEX's route to becoming a Chartered Legal Executive lawyer, read directly from cilex.org.uk and itemised on 2026-09-27. CPQ Foundation comprises six modules, all mandatory (there is no optional-unit choice at this stage; optionality begins at CPQ Advanced): F1 Legal Systems, F2 The Law of Tort, F3 Contract Law, F4 Introduction to Property and Private Client, F5 Professional and Legal Skills (Succeeding in the Legal Environment) and F6 Professional and Legal Skills (Legal Research). CPQ Foundation is the RQF Level 3 stage that replaced the legacy, separately-regulated CILEx Level 3 Diploma in Law and Practice (601/3417/3, closed to new registrations) from 2021; successful completion is what now leads to CILEX Paralegal status and progression to CPQ Advanced. Assessment: F1, F2, F3 and F4 are each a 2-hour, 80-mark, online remote-invigilated exam of 60 multiple-choice and short automated questions. F5 (2h30, 40 marks) has a knowledge section on succeeding in the legal environment plus a practical effective-communication exercise. F6 (2h30, 60 marks) has a section on research process/methods plus a section on research analysis and reporting. Stage tests and the mock in this course are original questions in CILEX's style (knowledge items plus IRAC-style scenario/problem questions), not CILEX's own live exam questions.
level_source: RQF Level 3, per Ofqual's regulated-qualification record for the predecessor CILEx Level 3 Diploma in Law and Legal Skills (60172484) and CILEX's own description of CPQ Foundation as replacing that Level 3 stage

learner_notices.text: This course covers CPQ Foundation Stage only (CILEX's entry tier, F1-F6) -- the broad, practical introduction to law and legal practice that leads to CILEX Paralegal status. It does not cover CPQ Advanced Stage (the compulsory A1 Dispute Resolution and Litigation and A2 Criminal Law and Litigation modules, the A4/A5 skills modules, or the optional A6 Wills/Probate/Private Client, A7 Family Law and Practice, or A8 Business and Employment Law modules) or CPQ Professional Stage. Advanced Stage, which this course's syllabus explicitly requires as complete before it is available, is a separate, more advanced course, following this library's usual split between a certifying body's entry and advanced tiers.

This course states English and Welsh law as understood to be current in September 2026. Figures that change routinely (SDLT/LTT thresholds and rates, IHT nil-rate bands, court fees, AML/CPD requirements) and any pending reform should be checked against a live source (legislation.gov.uk, gov.uk, cilex.org.uk, HM Land Registry, HMRC) before relying on them in practice or in a real CILEX exam sitting. In particular: the Human Rights Act 1998 remains in force; a 'Bill of Rights Bill' that would have replaced it was introduced in 2022 but withdrawn in 2023 and never enacted, though CILEX's own F1 module material still names it as content to be aware of.

This course teaches the law of England and Wales, which CILEX's syllabus assumes. Most subjects here (contract, tort, the core criminal/civil court structure) are not devolved and apply identically in Wales. The clearest exception taught in this course is property taxation: standard Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) applies to land transactions in England, while Wales has its own devolved Land Transaction Tax (LTT), with different rates and bands set by the Welsh Government -- flagged where relevant in the Property and Private Client stages.

F2, F3 and F5 each make it an explicit learning outcome that a trainee recognises the limits of their own authority and knows when to seek assistance from a supervisor. Treat this as part of the substantive content, not a soft skill -- CILEX can examine it directly in a scenario question.
